problem: Object-goal navigation methods mostly only reach near an object and ignore framing it in the camera view. Grid-based VL maps like VLMaps are memory-heavy, hard to update, and prior knowledge fails under occlusion, displacement or localization error.
motivation: Household robots repeatedly operate in the same environment, so prior maps can guide them. They are low-compute, and the environment changes, so prior knowledge must be fused with current observations. The final pose must also show clearly which object the robot is looking at (legibility).
key_idea: Store CLIP embeddings on the SLAM pose graph (VLPG) to pick and cluster object viewpoints, center the object with a local-planner cost, and replan viewpoints via an object localization probability map when the object is not visible.
insight: The ablation (frontier exploration, VLPG only, VLPG+centering, full VLPG-Nav) shows each component adds value. Object centering cuts pixel and angular error, and local search recovers occluded cases like the oven, which all other baselines miss. SAE rises from 0.66 (VLPG) to 0.73 (+centering) to 0.85 (full). Failures come mainly from wrong initial viewpoint clusters (Buddha statue).
method: VLPG construction: augments SLAM pose-graph nodes (x,y,θ) with CLIP image embeddings, adding a node about every 100 ms only if its cosine similarity to all existing embeddings is below ε; about 2000×512 for a 10×10 m environment, roughly 20x smaller than a VLMap.

Initial viewpoint guess: computes CLIP cosine similarity of 'A photo of {object}' vs 'A photo of something else' against all nodes, takes top-k, clusters poses in (x,y,cosθ,sinθ) with DBSCAN, and picks the viewpoint in the largest cluster whose FoV overlaps most with the others.
Object detection: zero-shot CLIP (ResNet50) + GradCAM saliency thresholded into a bounding box, running at about 10 Hz.

Object centering: adds an orient cost (change in squared horizontal bbox-center error, predicted over the horizon with image-Jacobian visual servoing) and a zoom cost to the stochastic MPC local planner (Theta* global planner).
Object localization probability map: a 6×6 m local grid initialized from the occupancy map; each cluster viewpoint's FoV updates p_nl with a user-defined p_l*, and p_l = 1 − p_nl.

Local search replanning: samples poses and picks the one minimizing distance + quality (FoV probability) + obstacle-clearance cost; if the object is still not seen, multiplies p_l in the current FoV by 0.2 and replans until success or the maximum number of replans.

setting.training_data: none (training-free; uses pre-trained CLIP and a prior exploration run to build the VLPG)
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera + 2D pose + local occupancy grid map
setting.action_space: non-holonomic velocity control via MPC local planner following Theta* waypoints
setting.simulator: Gazebo + Unreal Engine (custom 2-bedroom house); Matterport3D scene for qualitative localization figure
setting.privileged: prior exploration of the environment (VLPG built beforehand); local occupancy map; object keyphrase assumed provided by an LLM; GT positions used only for evaluation

numbers.eval_set_note: 8 randomly selected objects in one simulated 2-bedroom house (Table 2 also lists dishwasher)
numbers.extra: prior exploration to build VLPG; 5 min time limit; success requires object in camera FoV
numbers.evidence: Table 2 last row: SAE (↑) 0.12 / 0.66 / 0.73 / 0.85 for Frontier / VLPG / VLPG+Obj. Centering / VLPG-Nav

numbers.eval_set_note: same 8 objects; ablation variant VLPG + Obj. Centering (Baseline 3)

numbers_note: Only SAE is aggregated; per-object pixel and angular errors are in Tables 1-2 (e.g., oven: 22 px / 22.2° only for VLPG-Nav). No standard benchmark results; real-world experiments are qualitative.
results: On 8 objects in a simulated home, VLPG-Nav gets SAE 0.85 vs 0.73 (VLPG+centering), 0.66 (VLPG only) and 0.12 (frontier exploration). It uniquely succeeds on the occluded oven, and the Buddha statue fails in simulation but succeeds on the real robot.
limitations: Local search depends on the quality of the initial top-k viewpoints; a wrong cluster (Buddha statue) cannot be recovered.
CLIP+GradCAM is noisy and produces imprecise attention maps/bounding boxes.
Tiny evaluation (8 objects, one environment, no standard benchmark); viewpoint replanning ignores non-holonomic dynamics; CLIP inference runs offboard on a laptop.
